subject.title: Codex app-server client closes before long maintenance turn completes; Gateway restart also terminates active turn without graceful recovery

question: For long Codex-backed maintenance turns interrupted by Gateway restart or app-server close, should OpenClaw resume the turn, send a durable restart-aware interruption/status notice, or keep the current retry-only failure guidance?
rationale: The code already has partial restart markers and narrow replay-safe retry, but the remaining behavior crosses transport failure classification, channel delivery, and side-effect-safe resumability policy.

options.title: Durable restart-aware notice first
options.body: Classify Gateway shutdown separately, deliver a channel-visible interruption/status notice after restart, and add resumability only for explicitly replay-safe states.

options.title: Full resumability
options.body: Invest in persisted maintenance-turn checkpoints and resume/synthesize final status across restarts, accepting broader state and replay-safety design work.

options.title: Keep retry-only guidance
options.body: Leave long-turn recovery manual and document the current failure semantics, accepting continued user-visible message loss during restart windows.

recommendation.title: Durable restart-aware notice first
recommendation.body: Classify Gateway shutdown separately, deliver a channel-visible interruption/status notice after restart, and add resumability only for explicitly replay-safe states.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and closed the latest restart-marker slice and are best positioned to decide whether the remaining behavior should become full recovery or a narrower interruption notice.
